gloss: to line up in a single row/line

definitions.gloss: to line up in a single row; to form a single line / queue
definitions.explanation: A standard expression for people or things arranging themselves in one line. Frequently used as an instruction in schools, ticket queues, and public transit, and to describe orderly formations.

examples.japanese: {一列|いちれつ}に{並|なら}んでください。
examples.english: Please line up in a single file.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちが{一列|いちれつ}に{並|なら}んで{歩|ある}いている。
examples.english: The children are walking in a single line.

examples.japanese: {改札|かいさつ}の{前|まえ}では{一列|いちれつ}に{並|なら}んでお{待|ま}ちください。
examples.english: Please wait in a single line in front of the ticket gate.

examples.japanese: {店|みせ}の{前|まえ}にお{客|きゃく}さんが{一列|いちれつ}に{並|なら}んで、{開店|かいてん}を{待|ま}っていた。
examples.english: Customers were lined up single-file in front of the shop, waiting for it to open.

notes:
Formed from {一列|いちれつ} ('one row, one line') + に (target particle) + {並|なら}ぶ ('to be lined up, to stand in a row'). The に marks the configuration the subject arranges into.

USAGE:
- Standard instruction in schools, theme parks, polling stations, train platforms, and anywhere orderly queuing is expected.
- Used both for people queuing (front-to-back) and for objects arranged side by side in one row.
- The causative/transitive version — arranging things in a line — is {一列|いちれつ}に{並|なら}べる.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一列|いちれつ}に{並|なら}んでください: please line up in one line
- {一列|いちれつ}に{並|なら}んで{待|ま}つ: to wait in a single line
- {一列|いちれつ}に{並|なら}んで{歩|ある}く: to walk in single file
- {一列|いちれつ}に{並|なら}べる: to arrange [things] in a single line (transitive)
- きれいに{一列|いちれつ}に{並|なら}ぶ: to line up neatly in a single row

RELATED WORDS:
- {二列|にれつ}に{並|なら}ぶ: to line up in two rows
- {縦一列|たていちれつ}に{並|なら}ぶ: to line up in a single vertical (front-to-back) line
- {横一列|よこいちれつ}に{並|なら}ぶ: to line up in a single horizontal row (side by side)
- {順番|じゅんばん}に{並|なら}ぶ: to line up in order / take turns in line
- {列|れつ}を{作|つく}る: to form a line / queue

TRANSITIVITY:
- {並|なら}ぶ is intransitive — the subject is what forms the line.
- {並|なら}べる is the transitive pair — used when someone actively arranges objects: {本|ほん}を{一列|いちれつ}に{並|なら}べた ('I lined up the books in a single row').
